title: Slice-core right fibrations detect cartesian colimits for a pullback-stable class
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and $\mathcal C$ fits in $\mathcal U'$. Use quasicategories, coherent diagrams, functor categories, mapping spaces, cores and limiting cones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the infinity category $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$ of $\mathcal U'$-small spaces of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], presentability of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and right and left fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Classification of a right fibration means classification of its opposite left fibration by [lem-coef-space-valued-straightening], with $\mathcal U'$ as its small universe and a further containing universe for the space category. Let $\mathcal C$ be a presentable infinity category relative to $\mathcal U$, with finite limits. Let $S$ be a replete class of morphisms of $\mathcal C$ stable under pullback: a pullback of a member of $S$ is in $S$. Replete means invariant under equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$.

A slice object over $x$ is an arrow $u\to x$, with coherent triangles over $x$ as morphisms and their coherent higher simplices; let $(\mathcal C_{/x})^S$ be its full subcategory on arrows in $S$. Define $\mathcal O^{(S)}_{\mathcal C}$ to be the simplicial subset of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$ consisting of simplices whose vertices are arrows in $S$ and whose edges are pullback squares. Target evaluation $\mathcal O^{(S)}_{\mathcal C}\to\mathcal C$ is a right fibration, with fiber over $x$ the core $((\mathcal C_{/x})^S)^{\simeq}$. Its classifying coherent functor is
$$\rho_S:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'},\qquad x\longmapsto((\mathcal C_{/x})^S)^{\simeq},$$
and its map on $f:x\to y$ is pullback $f^*$ on these cores, with all higher compatibilities. For $S$ the class of all arrows, write $\rho(x)=(\mathcal C_{/x})^{\simeq}$. For any small right cone $J^{\triangleright}$ and diagram $q:J^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$, pullback of an apex arrow $u\to q(\infty)$ gives a coherent transformation $q(-)\times_{q(\infty)}u\to q$ cartesian at all edges. Every transformation cartesian at all edges of this cone is equivalent over $q$ to this pullback transformation for its own apex arrow.

Assume colimits in $\mathcal C$ are universal: for every small colimit $D\to L$ and maps $L\to B\leftarrow T$, the cocone $D(j)\times_BT\to L\times_BT$ is colimiting. Let $K$ be a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set and $q:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ a colimit cocone. Then the following are equivalent:

(a) The coherent cone $\rho_S\circ q^{\mathrm{op}}:(K^{\triangleright})^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$ is limiting. Thus $\rho_S(q(\infty))$, with its specified pullback maps, is a limit of $\rho_S\circ(q|_K)^{\mathrm{op}}$ in the infinity category of spaces; only this specified limit is asserted.

(b) For every coherent transformation $\alpha:p\to q$ with $p$ also a colimit cocone, whose naturality squares at all edges of $K$ are pullbacks and whose components $\alpha(k)$ lie in $S$ for all vertices $k\in K$, the naturality squares at every edge of $K^{\triangleright}$ are pullbacks and $\alpha(\infty)$ lies in $S$.

The equivalence includes $K=\varnothing$, with the empty limit the one-point terminal space.

source.place: HTT Notation 6.1.3.4 (the right fibration of arrows and pullback squares); Lemmas 6.1.3.2-6.1.3.3 (cartesian cone as apex pullback); Lemma 6.1.3.5, equivalence (2) and (3), printed pp. 544-547; Corollary 3.3.3.3, printed p. 216, for the space-valued section/limit formulation. Read in sandbox HTT-second-reader.pdf. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: First construct the arrow fibration without using any of the assertions to be proved. Evaluation $\mathrm{ev}_1:\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)\to\mathcal C$ is an inner fibration: apply the restriction/isofibration clause of [lem-coef-infinity-parameter-cone-extension] to $\{1\}\subseteq\Delta^1$. The arrow mapping-space formula [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square] shows that a square over $f:x\to y$ is Cartesian for this projection exactly when its source object is the pullback of its target arrow along $f$: after fixing a map into $x$, the required mapping-space comparison is exactly $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(t,u)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(t,v)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(t,y)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(t,x)$ for every $t$. This is the pullback universal property. The dual of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] identifies this comparison with horn-Cartesianness. Finite limits provide such a lift with any prescribed target arrow; hence evaluation is a Cartesian fibration. Apply [lem-coef-cartesian-core-right-fibration]. Its Cartesian core consists precisely of pullback-square edges and has fiber $(\mathcal C_{/x})^{\simeq}$. Restrict to vertices in $S$: an inner or higher right horn already contains all vertices, whereas lifting a one-dimensional right horn adds the pullback of its prescribed target arrow. Pullback stability of $S$ supplies that missing vertex, and repleteness permits any equivalent pullback choice. The restriction is therefore a right fibration with the stated restricted-core fibers.

Apply the opposite of [lem-coef-space-valued-straightening], in universe $\mathcal U'$, to the right fibration just constructed. The fiber formula gives $\rho_S(x)$, and the Cartesian-core transport formula of step 1 gives precisely pullback along $f:x\to y$, including the higher compatibilities from straightening. Taking all arrows gives $\rho$. For any diagram on $J^{\triangleright}$, the inclusion of its apex is right anodyne: in [lem-coef-infinity-cone-mono-right-anodyne] take $A=\varnothing$ and $B=J$. By [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation], a lift of this diagram to the all-arrows right fibration with a prescribed apex arrow has a contractible space of choices. Each component square into the apex is a pullback by step 1, so its source at $j$ is $q(j)\times_{q(\infty)}u$. This proves existence and coherent uniqueness of the asserted pullback transformation, and identifies every cartesian transformation on the cone with this one for its own apex. This proves the introductory classification and cartesian-cone assertions rather than assuming them.

For $J=K$ or $K^{\triangleright}$ let $\mathcal A_J$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal C)_{/q|_J}$ on cartesian transformations with all vertex components in $S$. Its core is the section space $\Gamma_J(\mathcal O^{(S)}_{\mathcal C},q)$: a section is just a cartesian transformation, and a parameter edge in the section space is a pullback square over an identity, hence an equivalence of slice objects. Conversely a componentwise equivalence between such transformations gives these pullback squares; [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] identifies componentwise equivalences with equivalences in the functor category. This accounts for every parameter simplex, since the defining condition is imposed on every edge. By [lem-coef-right-fibration-cone-section-criterion], condition (a) is equivalent to restriction $\mathcal A_{K^{\triangleright}}^{\simeq}\to\mathcal A_K^{\simeq}$ being an equivalence of spaces.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.3.5, space/core version of the categories in its proof; Corollary 3.3.3.3

proof.text:
Let $\mathcal B$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\mathcal C)_{/q}$ on transformations $\alpha:p\to q$ for which $p$ is colimiting and $\alpha|_K$ belongs to $\mathcal A_K$. Restriction $\mathcal B\to\mathcal A_K$ is an equivalence. Here are its mapping-space and existence arguments. Write $D=p|_K$ and $D'=p'|_K$. The dual of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] identifies the space of maps between these cocones with
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(D,D')\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(D,\Delta_Kp'(\infty))}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(p(\infty),p'(\infty)).$$
The cocone mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes the last factor's map to the base an equivalence because $p$ is colimiting. Thus restriction on maps is an equivalence. Taking its homotopy fibers over maps to the fixed cocone $q$ gives the same assertion in the slice, including all commuting-triangle homotopies. For a given $D\to q|_K$ in $\mathcal A_K$, presentability supplies a colimit cocone $p$ on $D$. Its universal property extends the composite $D\to q|_K\to\Delta_Kq(\infty)$ to $p(\infty)\to q(\infty)$ in a contractible space; the same displayed formula gives a coherent transformation $p\to q$. This proves essential surjectivity. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to this fully faithful functor: its full essential image is all of $\mathcal A_K$, so it has a coherent quasi-inverse. Consequently restriction induces an equivalence $\mathcal B^{\simeq}\to\mathcal A_K^{\simeq}$, not merely surjectivity on objects.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.3.5, the restriction from colimit extensions; Proposition 4.3.2.15 replaced by its cocone mapping-space argument

proof.text: There is a full inclusion $\mathcal A_{K^{\triangleright}}\subseteq\mathcal B$. Indeed step 2 identifies an object on the left with pullback along its apex arrow $u\to L$, where $L=q(\infty)$. Apply the assumed universality of colimits to $D=q|_K$, its colimit $L$, and $L\xrightarrow{1}L\leftarrow u$. It makes the cocone $q(k)\times_Lu\to L\times_Lu\simeq u$ colimiting. The equivalence from step 2 then makes the original source cocone colimiting, as the cocone mapping-space criterion is invariant under equivalences. Its restriction already has the required cartesian squares and $S$-components. This proves the inclusion using precisely the universality hypothesis.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.3.5, inclusion of Cartesian cone extensions in colimit extensions; Lemma 6.1.3.3(1) implies (5)

proof.text: The restriction in step 3 factors as the core of the full inclusion in step 5 followed by the equivalence in step 4. Thus (a) holds exactly when that inclusion on cores is an equivalence. If (a) holds, every $\alpha\in\mathcal B$ is equivalent over $q$ to an object of $\mathcal A_{K^{\triangleright}}$. Equivalences are componentwise by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The pullback universal-property comparison remains an equivalence after such componentwise equivalences, and repleteness preserves membership of the apex in $S$. Hence $\alpha$ itself is cartesian on the cone and its apex belongs to $S$, which is (b). Conversely (b) says exactly that every object of $\mathcal B$ belongs to $\mathcal A_{K^{\triangleright}}$. Both are full subcategories of the same slice, so their inclusion is then an equality on objects and all simplices. Its core is therefore an equivalence, and steps 3-4 give (a). The full-subcategory argument supplies the higher uniqueness that an objectwise existence argument alone would miss.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.3.5, explicit (2) implies (3) and (3) implies (2) using cores

proof.text: For $K=\varnothing$, $L$ is initial and $\mathcal A_K^{\simeq}$ is the one-point space. Universality applied to $L\xrightarrow{1}L\leftarrow u$ shows that the source $u$ of every arrow into $L$ is initial. Therefore the whole slice over $L$ has contractible core: every arrow is equivalent to $1_L$ and is terminal in the slice. The nonempty full subcategory of terminal objects is contractible by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Repleteness implies that the restricted core is either empty (if $1_L\notin S$) or this contractible core (if $1_L\in S$). Thus (a) holds exactly when $1_L\in S$. In (b) there are no squares to test and both source and target apexes are initial; every possible apex arrow is equivalent to $1_L$. Hence (b) has exactly the same condition. In particular pullback stability alone has not been mistaken for membership of $1_L$ in $S$. The point shape gives restriction an equivalence by step 2, as another check.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.3.5, empty-shape verification; Lemma 6.1.3.6, strict initial object

proof_origin.place: Expanded proof of Lemma 6.1.3.5(2) iff (3), with the general Cartesian-core and right-fibration section criteria as separate supporting nodes. Read the online PDF; not archived in literature/.
